findings.claim: Right Action is described as "The sixth step of the Noble Eightfold Path" in the glossary definition, the in-text term definition and a flashcard answer.
findings.truth: Right Action is the fourth factor of the Noble Eightfold Path (view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, concentration). L3 of this same unit correctly makes Right Livelihood the fifth, so the unit contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Noble Eightfold Path (fetched); internal cross-check with L3 content_html and glossary

findings.claim: "Examiners report that most mark loss happens here, and that the most common failures are..."
findings.truth: No such examiner report is cited or citable. The advice that follows is sound, so only the invented attribution is removed.
findings.evidence: fabricated examiner claim - checker brief, exam-claims rule

findings.claim: "The two named non-religious organisations in this theme are Humanist UK ... and Amnesty International" and "both named in the spec for this theme - use them."
findings.truth: The human-rights theme's set content names neither organisation. Its preamble asks only for scripture and other sources of authority; the phrase about the beliefs of Humanists and Atheists sits in the life-and-death theme, not this one. Non-religious views are still creditable, so the wording is softened rather than removed.
findings.evidence: spec pp. 29-33 (theme 4, all six perspectives) vs p. 16 (life and death preamble); grep for 'Humanist'/'Amnesty' across the spec

findings.claim: "Christian Aid and church food banks are cited in the spec as examples of this in action."
findings.truth: The set content names Christian Aid for the Christian perspective. Church food banks are not named.
findings.evidence: spec p. 29, Christian perspective, issues of wealth and poverty

findings.claim: Every 15-mark model mark scheme ends "[15 marks + 5 SPaG]" (L1, L2 and L3).
findings.truth: This paper carries 6 marks for spelling, punctuation and grammar, not 5 (12 across the qualification, split between the two written papers that assess it).
findings.evidence: spec p. 9 assessment block ('120 marks (plus 6 for spelling, punctuation and grammar)') and p. 60 SPaG statement

findings.field: content_html, conclusion_html, exam_tip_html, practice_questions, knowledge_checks, flashcard_questions, glossary_terms
findings.claim: The organisation is called "Humanist UK" throughout L4 (11 places, including a glossary term and a multiple-choice option).
findings.truth: The organisation is Humanists UK, renamed from the British Humanist Association in May 2017. L1 and L2 of this unit already use the correct name.

findings.claim: "The Humanist view is that rights are grounded in a situationist or relativist framework", repeated in a mark scheme as "the situationist/relativist approach vs religious absolutism".
findings.truth: Humanists UK campaigns for human rights as universal and supports the UDHR as a universal framework. L1 of this unit says exactly that, so the unit contradicts itself. Humanists judge acts by their effect on people rather than by scripture, which is what the sentence should say.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with L1 content_html; Humanists UK campaigning position

findings.claim: "Which British secular organisation campaigns against torture, political imprisonment and the death penalty worldwide?" with Humanists UK offered as a distractor.
findings.truth: Amnesty International is an international organisation. 'British' fits the distractor better than the keyed answer, so the stem misleads.
findings.evidence: Amnesty International is a global movement with an international secretariat; Humanists UK is the British body

findings.claim: "Sewa - selfless service - is one of the three pillars of Sikhism (alongside naam japna and kirat karo)."
findings.truth: The three daily duties are naam japna, kirat karo and vand chhakna (sharing with others). Sewa is a central Sikh practice, not the third duty.

findings.claim: "Christian Aid works across more than 50 countries."
findings.truth: Christian Aid works in about 24 countries. Replaced with 'more than 20 countries', which stays true as the figure moves.

findings.claim: The 15-mark question in L1, L2 and L3 is set as "Evaluate this statement. In your answer you should: refer to religious teaching; give reasoned arguments to support this statement; give reasoned arguments to support a different point of view; reach a justified conclusion."
findings.truth: That four-bullet instruction is another board's evaluation rubric. The tariff (15) is right for this paper, but the instruction is not: this paper's evaluation question asks the candidate to consider more than one point of view and to refer to religion and belief. L4 already uses that form, so the unit is inconsistent. Rewritten in house wording, not the board's.
findings.evidence: spec pp. 8-9 assessment section (four compulsory themes, 120 marks); house copyright-distancing rule

findings.claim: "the spec also notes that some Buddhist monks in Myanmar have been associated with the 969 Movement".
findings.truth: The set content is the opposite: Buddhist monks in Myanmar promoting tolerance towards Muslims in light of the 969 Movement. Both facts are real, but a student revising from this lesson would offer the wrong example, and the specification is misquoted.
findings.evidence: spec p. 33, Buddhist perspective, prejudice and discrimination

findings.claim: A mark scheme opens "Award one mark for each of two correct examples from:".
findings.truth: House rule bans board rubric phrasing of this shape. L1-L3 already use the neutral form 'One mark each for any two from:'.
findings.evidence: house copyright-distancing rule; internal consistency with L1-L3

findings.claim: Every 15-mark model answer attaches SPaG marks to that question, in all four lessons.
findings.truth: The spec says SPaG is assessed in specified extended-writing questions and gives 6 marks for this paper. It does not say every 15-mark question carries them; on a real paper the 6 marks sit on designated question(s). Options: (a) keep '+ 6 SPaG' on each 15-mark model answer, which teaches the right total and the right question type; (b) mark only one per set and add a line that SPaG is assessed on specified extended-writing questions. Recommend (a), which is what the fixes deliver.
findings.ruling: Accepted as delivered by the edits (+6 SPaG on the 15-mark model answers).

findings.claim: "condemned across all six traditions covered in this course" and a survey of all six perspectives in every lesson.
findings.truth: The spec sets this theme from six perspectives, but a candidate studies Christianity plus one other religion. The breadth is not wrong for a public revision site and it suits schools with different world-faith options, so no edit. Worth knowing if the unit is ever ported to a single school.
findings.evidence: spec pp. 28-33; summary of assessment pp. 2-3

findings.claim: The exam tip offers "Buddha-nature (Buddhism)" as the concept that grounds human dignity.
findings.truth: The set content for the Buddhist perspective is the Five Precepts and the Eightfold Path, which is what the lesson body uses. Buddha-nature is a Mahayana idea and is not wrong, but it is not the safest thing to name.
findings.evidence: spec p. 33, Buddhist perspective, human rights and social justice

findings.claim: Flashcard answer "Agree paragraph (named source), disagree paragraph (contrasting source), weighing language, justified conclusion."
findings.truth: This is a comma list, which the flashcard validator rejects. Not a fact error, so left alone; flagged in case a validation pass runs over the unit after the edits land.

summary: Scripture, law, dates and named figures check out across all four lessons (Genesis 1:26-27, Galatians 3:28 verbatim NIV, Acts 10:34-35, Qur'an 5:32/5:8/49:13/2:177, Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5, Catechism paragraph ranges, UDHR 1948, Equality Act 2010, King 1929-1968 and the 1963 letter, Khalsa 1699, Ambedkar 1956, HIAS 1881, zakat as the third Pillar at 2.5%), and every knowledge-check key is correct. The real damage is elsewhere: one HIGH factual error (Right Action placed sixth rather than fourth on the Eightfold Path, in three fields), an invented examiner report, two false claims that the specification names things it does not, a wrong Christian Aid figure, sewa put in place of vand chhakna, the wrong name for Humanists UK throughout L4, and the 15-mark questions carrying another board's rubric with 5 SPaG marks instead of 6.
